title: Interaction Between Gut Microbiota and TKIs in Defining the Clinical Outcomes of Patients With CML
official: Interaction Between Gut Microbiota and Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Defining the Clinical Outcomes of Patients With Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
summary: Gut microbiome (GM) is acquiring increasing importance in human health and disease. GM influences hematopoiesis and immune cells types differentiation. Patients with cancer are characterized by dysbiosis and compromised immunity. In the case of Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML), treatment with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (TKIs) restores immunosurveillance; in particular deep molecular response (DMR) is associated with increased levels of NK and CD8+ Tcells. There is no literature on the effects of GM on CML outcomes. This project aims to identify a microbial signature associated with a higher probability of achieving DMR.

interventions.name: non interventional study with the use of biological samples.
